Prompt B, new conversation: Image 1 is the exact layout. Use it as the structure for a scientifically accurate horizontal cross-section of the lower face at the level of the mandibular foramen, seen from above, with the lips at the top: keep every outline, position and size exactly as drawn, in the same 4:3 landscape frame, with the tissue running to the left, right and bottom edges and the plain off-white space above the lips left plain. Exact labels, a syringe and a needle will be laid over it afterwards.

Image 2 is for understanding the anatomy only: how the inferior alveolar nerve, artery and vein lie in the pterygomandibular space between the ramus of the mandible and the medial pterygoid, with the lingual nerve in front of and medial to them, and the pterygomandibular raphe where the buccinator meets the superior constrictor. Image 2 is drawn the other way up; follow image 1 for every side and direction. Take the relationships from image 2; take every position, shape and size from image 1; the drawing itself is new.

Paint it as a premium anatomy-atlas plate: a rich, deep, saturated palette with soft glossy highlights, fine crisp outlines and gentle depth, lit softly from the upper left.

Work from the outside in:
1. The skin is a thin pink layer around the face, over golden subcutaneous fat with fine pale septa.
2. The masseter muscles at the sides and the medial pterygoid muscles inside the rami are deep maroon muscle cut across its fibres, with fine white connective-tissue streaks. The buccinator, the dark red band inside each cheek, and the superior constrictor, the band curving round the back of the mouth to the throat, are the same muscle in thin bands.
3. The rami of the mandible are bone cut across: a smooth ivory cortex around pale spongy bone.
4. The parotid glands behind the rami are pale tan lobulated gland.
5. The pterygomandibular space, the pale wedge inside the right ramus, is soft loose yellow fat. In it, the inferior alveolar nerve is a small round olive-yellow nerve with a pale sheath and fine fascicles, with a small red artery and a small blue vein beside it; the lingual nerve in front of it is a smaller nerve drawn the same way.
6. The raphes are small pale glistening tendinous knots where buccinator meets constrictor.
7. The lower teeth are enamel crowns in section, smooth ivory-white with a soft sheen, set in pink gum; the tongue is a large rounded mass of pink-red muscle with a velvety surface; the oral lining is moist pink mucosa; the throat is a dark airway at the bottom centre.

The picture shows only this anatomy.
